effect: DEBUG MENU (13 game settings), then a game with them (hold L, R, Up on the right pad and Left on the left pad while pressing A)
note: The last two entries of the button-code list ($27EB6). The check ($0702_00F0) wants pad bits L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left; with them held in BizHawk the [ DEBUG MENU ] opens with 13 settings, and A starts a game with them. GameFAQs doesn't have it.

effect: DEBUG MENU, then a game where the CPU plays both sides (hold L, R, Up on the right pad and Left on the left pad while pressing A)
note: The last two entries of the button-code list ($27EB6). The check ($0702_00F0) wants pad bits L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left; with them held in BizHawk the [ DEBUG MENU ] opens with 13 settings, and A starts a game with them; unlike 0825 (this is sub-mode 3, $0700_6D64) your side is CPU-controlled too, so both fields play themselves and the round replays. GameFAQs doesn't have it.

effect: Your pad moves both sides: the opponent's field follows your Left and Right (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E8; the opponent's control word becomes 1 instead of $101 ($0700_6DDE), so player 1's pad drives both fields and the CPU never moves. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held: both falling pieces move together.

effect: A RESULT screen after every round: level, chains, giant bombs, stage times (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E0; after each round the main loop calls the RESULT screen ($0700_7E46) that normally comes only after the ending. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held.

effect: Other block pieces in every game
note: Sets $0500_24F4; a normal game then uses piece set (TUBU) 5 instead of its own ($0700_7C1A). Typed in BizHawk.

effect: DOKURO blocks in every game: the attack rows you get are brick blocks instead of Bomberman heads (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E4, which turns DOKURO ($0500_2540) on at every stage start ($0700_7BBA): the 8-block attack row uses block kind $B instead of 6 ($0700_97F2). Clearing one next to a chain releases an item ($0701_2322 -> $0701_5E14). Typed in BizHawk with L and R held, then Normal, The Scary Ruins: the CPU's chains sent brick rows into your field. Image: without the code (left) and with it.

effect: Fewer idle animations in every game: the blocks in the fields blink and wink half as often (hold L and R while entering)
note: Clears $0500_2500, so ANIMATION ($0500_24C4) is 0 instead of 1. $0700_EC68 starts a block's idle animation on a random cell; ANIMATION 0 tries on every 4th frame, 1 on every 2nd, 2 on every frame. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held and counted over 5,000 frames: with the code every start fell on one frame in four, without it on two.

effect: Developer menu at power-on: VERSION 1995/07/21 with GAME START, DEBUG GAME PLAY, DEBUG AUTO PLAY, SOUND TEST, ENDING
note: The menu ($0700_0A48) is in the ROM but nothing calls it. The patch calls it from boot mode 0 (file $06B2) and points its three debug items at the sub-mode word the finished game reads ($0500_24F8; they still wrote the old byte $0500_26D9). Patched file in BizHawk: GAME START boots normally, DEBUG GAME PLAY and DEBUG AUTO PLAY give the DEBUG MENU then a game (as 0825 and 0513), SOUND TEST and ENDING open those.

effect: SCROLL, ANIMATION, DOKURO, TUBU, ENEMY, WORLD, SPEED, COLOR, ERASE, ITEM, EVENT, WIN, CPU: the 13 values a stage normally sets for you
note: Left-pad Right and Left change a value. SCROLL background scroll on/off; ANIMATION how often blocks start an idle animation (0 every 4th frame, 1 every 2nd, the normal value, 2 every frame); DOKURO brick attack rows, which drop items when cleared; TUBU piece set 0-5; ENEMY the opponent 0-10; WORLD the background 0-3; SPEED drop speed 0-5; COLOR block kinds 1-5; ERASE blocks in a row to clear 1-6; ITEM n makes every item type n-1 (items come only from DOKURO blocks); EVENT n forces event n-1 and makes a 2-chain enough to start it, for the left player only (a giant spiked robot, rolling explosions, a vortex, a red flood); WIN the round wins that end a match (1, the default, or 2); CPU the opponent's level (0F chains and attacks fast, 00 only clears). All seen in BizHawk (menu $0700_64B0, stage tables from $0702_6588).

effect: A forced event on your first 2-chain: a giant spiked robot, rolling explosions, a vortex, or a red flood that refills the field
note: EVENT n > 0 sets the chain thresholds $254A/$254C to 1 and 2 (normally 4 and 5) and forces event n-1, but only for the left player (struct $5954, whose +8 is 0), so the CPU opponent of 0825 never starts one; with 0513 the left side plays itself. In BizHawk with CPU 0F: each event started on the left side's 2-chain. Image: EVENT 1, 2 (top), 3, 4.

effect: Every item is one type: ITEM n gives type n-1, 16 items in all
note: Items come only from cleared DOKURO brick rows, and their type is normally random & 15 ($0701_5FEC); the effects are a switch at $0701_6632 and work on the owner's field. ITEM 1 bricks become bombs; 2 left and right swapped for about 500 frames; 3 pieces fall at full speed for about 500 frames; 4 blasts use level 0 for about 500 frames (from the code); 5 bombs become rocks; 6 every bomb explodes; 7 the next piece is a giant bomb; 8 a big Bomberman bounces in front of your field; 9 a row of bricks pushed up; 10 four rocks pushed up; 11 STOP: a 5-4-3-2-1 countdown with no pieces falling; 12 bricks drop into the outer columns; 13 the next piece is rocks; 14 every face block cleared; 15 a row of bombs pushed up; 16 every bomb removed. In BizHawk with 0513, DOKURO 1 and CPU 0F: each icon seen, and each effect seen in the field except 2-4 and 16 (seen in RAM). Image: ITEM 1-8 (top) and 9-16.

code: Title screen: right-pad Left, B, right-pad Down, A, right-pad Up
effect: A test screen: one horizontal line for the left eye, two short vertical bars for the right
note: $0701_B1DC follows the sequence on the PANIC BOMBER title (any other new press starts it over) and sets the main mode $0500_26D6 = 6 ($0701_B270), which runs $0701_7E74. Seen together, the bars cross the line: it looks like a chart for lining up the two screens. A or Start goes back to the intro ($0701_7FF2). Entered before the demo starts, seen in MAME (both eyes; image: left eye, right eye) and BizHawk (left eye).

code: Hold A, B, L, R, Start and Select during the ending
effect: Skips the ending scenes: the castle door and the statue end at once
note: Mode 7 ($0701_8088) checks the held buttons at each scene's steps ($0701_87EA): with exactly A, B, L, R, Start and Select held (and no d-pad) it ends the scene ($0700_63EE). In BizHawk after a real Doom Castle win: the door scene ended after about 38 frames instead of 525 and the bonus stage began; at the statue, about 37 frames instead of about 966, straight to RESULT.

effect: Tunes and effects the game never plays, some out of the sound test's reach
note: Music goes through $0700_63B8 (table $0707_4024, 00-15) and effects through $0700_63C8 (table $0707_4080, 00-28). Tune 0E and effects 00 and 1F are never requested; only the sound test plays them. Tunes 13-15 and effects 24-28 are past the test's range (BGM 0-12, SE 0-23), so nothing can play them. 0E is a full tune; 13 and 14 two versions of another; 15 a short rising run into a held note, likely a test tone. The effects last 0.2 to 0.8 s. Recorded in MAME.
